tra_loi.Q1: The British. A Union Jack flies over the stone tower and walls of the town on the Rock in frames 40–41 (Jan 1780). The pictures don't show how or when they got it.
tra_loi.Q2: "1779 — The Great Siege" (the caption in frame 23). Camps and trench lines appear on the land side, and ships gather in the bay.
tra_loi.Q3: Not sure. The pictures never show hunger directly. A blockade seems to be the cause: camps and a trench line on land, and ships sitting off the town. I saw no food, no starving people and no text about hunger.
tra_loi.Q4: A relief fleet of ships. A group of sailing ships arrives in the bay on 18 Jan 1780 (frame 47), and people unload supplies on the quay or mole in frames 48–49 (22 and 26 Jan 1780). The pictures don't say who they are or exactly what they bring. A different, larger fleet of ships sits offshore in April 1781 (frames 53–59), and it could be a relief fleet or an attacker.

tra_loi.Q1: The British hold it. A Union Jack flies on the tower and walls above the town (frames 40-41, 51). The pictures do not name the nation outright. Two camps sit on the plain outside, with a line of troops between them and the Rock, and they appear to be the besiegers.
tra_loi.Q2: A siege of the Rock. The caption 'The Great Siege' appears at frame 23, dated 21 Jun 1779. Two camps and a line of troops then build up on the land side, and ships gather in the bay.
tra_loi.Q3: Not sure. The pictures never show hunger or food shortage directly. The likely reason is the blockade, because ships sit offshore and camps and a troop line cut off the land side. I am inferring that from the setup, not from any frame that shows starvation.
tra_loi.Q4: Ships. A fleet of sailing ships approaches the bay on 18 Jan 1780 (frame 47), and a larger fleet is in the bay in April 1781 (frames 53-56). A single ship sails in earlier, in frames 36-39. The pictures do not clearly show the ships delivering supplies or fighting, so I read them as a relief fleet but am not certain.

tra_loi.Q1: The British. A Union Jack flies on the tower and walls at frames 40-41 (14 Jan 1780), and the town is shown holding out under siege. Nothing on screen names the besiegers' nation.
tra_loi.Q2: The Great Siege. The caption at frame 23 reads '1779 — The Great Siege' (21 Jun 1779). Camps, trench lines and ships then surround the Rock.
tra_loi.Q3: Not clearly shown. The pictures suggest a blockade: ships ring the harbour and land camps cut the Rock off, and a lone ship is seen sailing in or out. No frame shows starvation or empty food stores, and the town just looks quiet. Hunger is inferred, not seen.
tra_loi.Q4: A fleet of ships. Frame 47 (18 Jan 1780) shows a group of ships sailing in, and frame 52 shows a single ship approaching the fort. Frames 53-56 show many ships near the town. Nothing shows clearly that these are relief ships rather than attackers, or whether they carry supplies.
